topic: Particle Technology Forum: 30 Years in Perspective
title: Particle Technology Forum: 30 Years in Perspective
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: In commemorating the 30 year anniversary of the formation of the AIChE Particle Technology Forum (PTF), I would like, as the Founding Chair (1992-1994), to share some reflections on the circumstances surrounding the genesis of this organization and recognize those pioneering researchers who shared the same vision for it and who devoted their time, energy and talent to realizing its inception. In celebrating the achievement signaled by this important milestone, I would like to offer my thoughts about this field and its topics of emphasis which are in the midst of transformation as well as the new and rising generation of engaged researchers. I will also discuss the efforts required to ensure the continued impact of the field on both academia and industry.

topic: The Particle Technology Forum: Success, but more to do
title: The Particle Technology Forum: Success, but more to do
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: AIChE has long been the leader in promoting the science of particle technology starting with being the first engineering society to offer a short course on storage and flow of powders and bulk solids in the 70s. This leadership position expanded dramatically with formation of the Particle Technology Forum 30 years ago. The author presents a look back on what has been accomplished and what more needs to be done.

topic: Influence of Mechanical Interlocking on the Flow Behavior of Granular Particles
title: Influence of Mechanical Interlocking on the Flow Behavior of Granular Particles
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: In order to obtain reliable predictions for the flow behavior of highly angular particles, such as Lunar and Martian soils, mechanical interlocking associated with sustained particle-particle interactions needs to be described. Mechanical interlocking gives rise to large particle-phase stress in granular soils and a significant resistance to deformation. In this study, the effect of particle interlocking in dilute and dense-phase granular flows is investigated via discrete element method (DEM) simulation of a 3D system of hook-shaped particles in simple shear flow using Lees-Edwards periodic boundary conditions. The effect of particle shape is assessed by progressively varying the degree of curvature of the hook-shaped particles. The particle shape varied from a straight, elongated particle to one in which the straight particle is folded in half. For each particle shape, a total normalized interlocking time and distribution of particle interlocks are determined over a range of solid concentrations. At low solid volume fractions, the normal and shear stresses are proportional to the inverse of the projected area of the particle in the plane perpendicular to the flow, consistent with the stress behavior of elongated particles [Guo et al., 2012]. For larger solid volume fractions, normal and shear stresses increases with increasing interlocking, showing a direct dependence between stress and degree of mechanical interlocking

title: How Standpipes Really Work
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: Standpipes have traditionally been thought of as a device which allows solids to be transferred from a low pressure to a higher pressure. Standpipes can certainly do this, but their true function is not so limited. The actual purpose of a standpipe is to adjust the pressure drop across them so that the pressure drops around the circulation loop are in balance. The four different types of standpipes and their operation will be reviewed. How each type of standpipe adjusts to balance the overall pressure drop in a circulation loop will be explained. Examples of standpipes adjusting to various operating conditions and solids flow rates will also be presented and described in detail.

topic: Persistence in the Face of Adversity to Achieve your Goals
title: Persistence in the Face of Adversity to Achieve your Goals
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: Excerpts will be taken from this open access paper published in Powder Technology ( https://doi.org/10.1016/j.powtec.2023.118279 ) as personal examples for how to overcome professional barriers along the way as you pursue your endeavors. The path from laboratory curiosities to commercial powder processing plants had many obstacles to overcome. The manner in which this was done can be applied to everyday life - be it obtaining a M.S. or Ph.D., pursuing a career afterwards, or simply living your life to the fullest in a very challenging world. PTF provides for an incredible opportunity to network with all kinds of people and is by far the most academic/industry integrated organization that I am aware of. Many “forks in the road” opportunities are available from being an active participant in PTF; so, I encourage you to be an active participant in this fantastic organization.

topic: Particle Technology in Tackling Global Challenges: Where are the opportunities
title: Particle Technology in Tackling Global Challenges: Where are the opportunities
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: Particle technology is a crucial field in the science and engineering of this age. It is particularly relevant to tackling global challenges such as carbon neutrality, public health and so on. On the other hand, it is facing disciplinary challenges in the research paradigm shift from being reductionism and average-based to being interdisciplinary and structure-based, a shift that better fills in the knowledge gaps at different levels. I am going to share with you what we have done over the past 40 years or so, covering the conceptual shift from multiscale to mesoscale, and then to mesoscience in the field of particle technology. I will first introduce why the average approach should be replaced by a multiscale approach, and why mesoscales at different levels are so crucial. I will then propose, with evidences from different cases, that the general principle of compromise in competition (CIC) is likely to exist for all mesoscales, leading to the conclusion that the concept of mesoscience refers not only to “scale”, but also to “regime”. Finally, I will give a mesoscale perspective for different disciplines and technological fields beyond its origin in particle technology. The presentation will conclude with the prospect of deducing simplicity and commonality from complexity and diversity. In essence, what we will probably achieve in mesoscience is crucial for more broadly tackling the global challenges and shifting the paradigm in science.

topic: Happy 30 th B’day PTF: A personal perspective on its international reach
title: Happy 30 th B’day PTF: A personal perspective on its international reach
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: For 25 years I have had the pleasure to benefit from the PTF’s community, grow with it, and serve it in various roles, while being in academic positions from TU Delft in the Netherlands (1998-2006) to Rensselaer in the USA (2006-2012) and UCL in the UK now, with particle technology related collaborations in other countries and continents. Through the lens of one of the AIChE Inter national Committee’s founding members, I will discuss the importance of the PTF from an international perspective, as the PTF has always been uniquely welcoming and embracing international participation. It has been an inclusive home for particle technology’s academic and industrial researchers and practitioners from around the world, at any stage of their career, especially through the events at the AIChE annual meeting with global participation. This has led to important exchanges that have shaped our field, but also social interactions that have given the PTF a human face. At 30 years young, the PTF is thriving as the global home for the particle technology community.
presenting_author: Marc-Olivier Coppens | University College London, United Kingdom
authors: Marc-Olivier Coppens | University College London, United Kingdom

topic: Particle Technology: Reflection from Canadian Activities
title: Particle Technology: Reflection from Canadian Activities
session_title: Invited: Celebrating 30 years of the PTF (The first 15 years)
abstract: This presentation will discuss some examples in particle science and engineering activities that are currently taking place in Canada and will reflect on the past, present, and future endeavors in the research and technology development in this field. Many research and development activities in Canada are directly associated with its vast nature resources, including tar sands, oil shale, and biomass with particle technology being their enabling technology for its commercial success. Academic and industrial interaction has been an important part of these efforts. Some examples surrounding the prolific interactions of researchers between Canadian organizations and the AIChE Particle Technology Forum on education and research in the field will be presented.
